package_info.why_malicious: This report does not analyze a specific malicious package or code, but rather describes a machine learning-based methodology for detecting anomalous and potentially risky author behavior in open-source software repositories. The focus is on identifying authors whose commit patterns deviate from their established norms, which may indicate account compromise or malicious intent.

behavioral_signatures: Sudden changes in commit timing (e.g., commits at unusual hours for the author)
Commits to new or previously untouched projects by an established author
High percentage of commits flagged as anomalous by behavioral clustering
Commits from an author shortly after a known account breach
file_indicators: No direct file indicators; detection is based on commit metadata and behavioral patterns
network_indicators: No direct network indicators; detection is based on version control system activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor commit metadata (timestamp, project, author) for each author over time. Use unsupervised clustering (e.g., DBSCAN) to establish a baseline of normal commit behavior for each author. Flag commits that fall outside established behavioral clusters as anomalous. Combine the proportion of anomalous commits with the total number of commits to identify high-risk authors. Correlate with other signals (e.g., password breach data, sudden project/language changes) for higher confidence in risk assessment.
